statement: A sequence is defined by $u_{1}=2$ and $u_{n+1}=\dfrac{2u_{n}}{1+u_{n}}$ for $n\ge1$. Find a formula for $u_{n}$ in terms of $n$, and find $\lim_{n\to\infty}u_{n}$.
solution: Let $v_{n}=1/u_{n}$. Then $v_{n+1}=\dfrac{1+u_{n}}{2u_{n}}=\tfrac12+\tfrac12v_{n}$, with $v_{1}=\tfrac12$. This linear recurrence has fixed point $1$, and $v_{n}-1=(\tfrac12)^{n}$, so $v_{n}=1-2^{-n}$ and $u_{n}=\dfrac{1}{1-2^{-n}}=\dfrac{2^{n}}{2^{n}-1}$. Hence $\lim_{n\to\infty}u_{n}=1$.
hints: Take reciprocals to linearise the recurrence.
